title: BSG Forecasting — Automated Business Strategy Game
subtitle: ML-driven competitor forecasting and Playwright execution for McGraw-Hill's Business Strategy Game
description: Two-stack ML + RPA automation for the McGraw-Hill Business Strategy Game capstone. A Python neural net layer (GradientBoosting + RandomForest + MLP, with scipy.optimize.differential_evolution for combinatorial decision search) generates optimal moves; a TypeScript + Playwright layer logs into bsg-online.com and drives the live game UI.
client: BSG capstone simulation (McGraw-Hill / Business Strategy Institute)
role: Solo developer of the ML + RPA automation; Team Lead of a 4-person company in the simulation.
technologies: Python, scikit-learn, scipy, TypeScript, Playwright, Vitest, Node.js
overview: BSG is a multi-year footwear-industry simulation used in undergraduate business capstones worldwide, with thousands of teams competing each term. I built a hybrid Python + TypeScript automation that turns the game into an optimization problem: parse the publisher's CIR / FIR / COR CSV exports, train per-company models that predict each competitor's next-year decisions, search the joint decision space for the best counter-strategy via differential evolution, then drive the live BSG web app via Playwright to apply those decisions year over year.
highlights: Multi-method ML ensemble: GradientBoostingRegressor + RandomForestRegressor + MLPRegressor for per-competitor decision prediction
Combinatorial decision optimization via scipy.optimize.differential_evolution
Playwright + TypeScript automation that logs into bsg-online.com and drives the live game UI
Vitest test coverage for the automation layer with per-team .env configs
Reveal.js review decks summarizing performance year over year
challenges: Modeling decision interaction effects rather than treating each lever in isolation
Driving a publisher web UI not built for automation — handling intermittent dropdowns, dialogs, and report rendering quirks
Parsing inconsistent CIR / FIR / COR CSV exports across years and industries
outcomes: Invited to the BSI conference as one of the top 100 teams worldwide (out of 3,700+).
Industry 26: rose from #8 to #1, $1.507B cumulative profit, EPS $16.49 vs $7.00 target.
Demonstrated end-to-end ML + RPA capability against a structured-game adversarial environment
results: Invited to the BSI conference as one of the top 100 teams worldwide (out of 3,700+). Industry 26 rose from #8 to #1 with $1.507B cumulative profit.
